title: A novel laboratory simulation system to uncover the mechanisms of uranium upward transport in a desert landscape
author: Zhang, Larson, et al.

steps.title: Dry soil in oven
steps.instruction: Place the collected soil in a drying oven and dry it completely before further processing.

steps.title: Grind dried soil
steps.instruction: Grind the dry soil using a ground plate and a grinding rod to obtain a fine material.

steps.title: Sieve soil to <2 mm
steps.instruction: Pass the ground soil through a 2 mm screen and collect the fraction that passes (<2 mm).

steps.title: Grind metal compounds
steps.instruction: Weigh the desired mass of each uranium compound (UO₂, UO₃, UO₂(NO₃)₂) and grind them separately into a fine powder with an agate mortar.

steps.title: Drill column holes
steps.instruction: Drill a series of 0.5 cm‑diameter holes along a column (diameter = 4 cm, height = 15 cm) from bottom to top, spacing the holes 2.5 cm apart.

steps.title: Prepare bottom cover and filter
steps.instruction: Drill 3 mm‑diameter holes in the bottom cover, place a filter paper on top of the bottom cover, and then place a thin layer of soil above the filter paper.

steps.title: Spread metal compounds on soil
steps.instruction: Weigh the appropriate amount of the powdered uranium compounds and uniformly spread them on the top surface of the soil layer that rests on the filter paper.

steps.title: Assemble column components
steps.instruction: Connect the soil column to the bottom section, ensuring the order: bottom cover → filter paper → thin soil layer → thin layer of uranium metal compounds.

steps.title: Pack soil to 5 cm height
steps.instruction: Add additional soil to the column until the packed height reaches 5 cm, applying a packing force of 20–25 N cm⁻² using a slide hammer.

steps.title: Immerse column bottom in solution
steps.instruction: Place the bottom of the packed column into an aqueous solution containing water and the desired companion cations/anions; ensure the uranium‑containing zone remains above the water level so that upward transport can occur by capillary rise during evaporation.

steps.title: Dry column in oven at 45 °C
steps.instruction: Put the column with wet soil into an oven set to 45 °C (simulating hot summer conditions in Yuma, AZ).

steps.title: Repeat wetting‑drying cycles
steps.instruction: Perform successive wetting (step 10) and drying (step 11) cycles until the soil column is completely dry (approximately 7 days); continue the cycles for the desired experimental period (e.g., 2 months).

steps.title: Sample lowest hole for XRF
steps.instruction: After the prescribed number of cycles (e.g., 2 months), remove the soil sample from the lowest drilled hole and measure its uranium concentration with an X‑ray fluorescence spectrometer (XRF).

steps.title: Monitor migration at other heights
steps.instruction: Periodically sample soil from the remaining holes at different column heights and analyze uranium concentration (e.g., by XRF) to track upward migration.

steps.title: Terminate cycles at target height
steps.instruction: Stop the wetting‑drying cycles when uranium is detected at the predetermined study height.

steps.title: Extract column intact
steps.instruction: Remove the entire soil column from the apparatus in one piece.

steps.title: Section column and subsample
steps.instruction: Cut the column into 2.5 cm thick layers and collect a 2 g mixed‑soil subsample from each layer for further analysis.

steps.title: Analyze U compounds by XRD
steps.instruction: Use X‑ray powder diffraction (XRD) to identify the uranium compounds present in each soil subsample.

steps.title: Perform SEM‑EDS analysis
steps.instruction: Run scanning electron microscopy (SEM) coupled with energy‑dispersive X‑ray spectroscopy (EDS) to examine morphology and elemental distribution in the samples.

steps.title: Fractionate uranium with SSD
steps.instruction: Apply the selective sequential dissolution (SSD) method to each soil section to determine uranium fractionation.

steps.title: Calculate transport rate
steps.instruction: Compute the uranium transport rate in the soil column based on the measured concentrations and the duration of the wetting‑drying cycles.

steps.title: Measure total U with XRF
steps.instruction: Measure total uranium concentrations in soils taken from the drilled holes using an X‑ray fluorescence spectrometer (Bruker).

steps.title: Acid digestion for ICP‑MS
steps.instruction: Digest soil for ICP‑MS analysis:

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1.0 g of soil into a 50 mL digestion tube (replicates).
Add 25 mL of 4 M HNO₃ and place the tube in a water bath at 80 °C for 16 h.
Decant the supernatant and filter it through a 0.45 µm filter.
Dilute the filtered digest to an appropriate volume.
Measure uranium (and other metal) concentrations in the diluted solution with ICP‑MS.
